claims.head: The Hurricanes should drive the play
claims.body: The Hurricanes have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Jets near the bottom. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Jets’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

claims.head: The Hurricanes hunt better looks than the Jets
claims.body: On shot quality, Carolina is one of the league’s best, but Winnipeg is one of the worst. The more dangerous chances should be the Hurricanes’.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 46% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 64 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (17 of 20 changes).

stakes: The Hurricanes go in first in the Metropolitan with 13 points, the Jets fourth in the Central with 10 points.

WPG.head: A tough matchup for the Jets
WPG.body: Even though Winnipeg has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Jets’ best way through is getting good looks.

CAR.head: Advantage, the Hurricanes
CAR.body: Even though Winnipeg has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Jets can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: Can anyone stop the Hurricanes?
paras: The Hurricanes are on a tear, six straight wins. The Jets are 4-1-2.
The Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Jets do. The Canes wait for good looks, but the Jets settle for hopeful ones.
